s1.syndrome_frame: Hyperlipidemia with variable response to treatment and potential issues with laboratory measurements
salient_findings: Discrepancy between direct and calculated LDL-C measurements
History of adverse effects from statins
key_facts: Patient is a 47-year-old African American man
Medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and gastroesophageal reflux disease
Patient has been tried on various statins
Patient experienced hip pain and elevated liver enzymes while on statins
Fasting lipid profile showed LDL-C of 232 mg/dL off lipid-lowering agents
Direct LDL-C was 113 mg/dL in June 2014
Direct LDL-C was 115 mg/dL in October 2015
Calculated LDL-C was 170 mg/dL in December 2015
Apolipoprotein B (Apo B) and Lipoprotein (a) [Lp(a)] were measured in 2016

shortlist.label: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated LDL-C levels and variable response to statins

shortlist.label: Familial Defective Apolipoprotein B
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated LDL-C levels and potential issues with laboratory measurements

shortlist.label: Lipoprotein(a) Hyperlipoproteinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Measurement of Lipoprotein(a) in 2016 and potential role in hyperlipidemia

shortlist.label: Familial Combined Hyperlipidemia
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of hyperlipidemia and variable response to treatment

shortlist.label: Hypertriglyceridemia-Induced Hyperlipidemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated triglycerides and potential secondary cause of hyperlipidemia

raw.rationale: The patient's significantly elevated LDL-C levels off lipid-lowering agents and the marked difference between direct and calculated LDL-C levels suggest a disorder affecting apolipoprotein B, which is a key component of LDL-C

rejected.label: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
rejected.why: While possible, the variable response to statins and the discrepancy between direct and calculated LDL-C levels may not be fully explained by this condition alone

rejected.label: Lipoprotein(a) Hyperlipoproteinemia
rejected.why: Although Lipoprotein(a) was measured, there's no direct indication it's elevated to a degree that would solely explain the patient's condition

rejected.label: Familial Combined Hyperlipidemia
rejected.why: This condition typically involves elevations in both cholesterol and triglycerides, but the primary issue here appears to be with LDL-C levels

rejected.label: Hypertriglyceridemia-Induced Hyperlipidemia
rejected.why: The patient's primary issue is with LDL-C, not triglycerides, making this diagnosis less likely
